claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II crew splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (0007 GMT April 11).
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II crew traveled around the Moon.
Recovery teams extracted the Artemis II crew shortly after splashdown.
The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed lunar mission return since 1972.
The Artemis II mission goal was a 10-day lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission tested Orion’s systems.
Splashdown time was Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT April 11).

The Artemis II crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch (mission specialist), and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist).
The crew was extracted from the Orion capsule via helicopter.
The crew was brought to the USS John P. Murtha.
The Orion capsule passed through 1000 ft before splashdown.
The Artemis II mission journey was 694,481 miles.
Parachutes were deployed in sequence—drogues followed by three main parachutes.
Parachutes reduced speed to approximately 20 mph (32 km/h).
